rationale: C11 plausibly supplied the child’s compact acknowledgment-of-report template: receipt or review of a recently transmitted report is followed by emphatic personal appreciation and a favorable statement about what the report demonstrates. The unusually close pairing of “report ... which you sent me” with “I am highly pleased” corresponds to the child’s “I appreciate most highly receiving the latest census reports.” C22 and C14 share economic-report subject matter and appreciative language, but their overlap is less distinctive and more generic.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I appreciate most highly receiving the latest census reports
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I have read with great interest the preliminary report ... which you sent me ... I am highly pleased
shared_material.explanation: Both use a first-person acknowledgment of a transmitted report immediately coupled with strongly favorable appreciation, including the conspicuous terms “highly” and “report.”

shared_material.child_excerpt: These figures confirm the facts ... that the American people are today better off than ever before in our history.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Publications such as the Commission recommends will greatly help to further this understanding.
shared_material.explanation: After acknowledging the report, both letters briefly state the broader national significance of the reported material, though this secondary parallel is structural rather than close verbal reuse.
